equipment_type: Gateway for Bender BMS-bus devices (insulation monitors, RCMs, changeover modules) - sensor/alarm data
applies_to: COM461MT software D402 V1.0x; the map is the gateway's process image, shown here for BMS device address 1 plus the built-in test record.
summary: The COM461MT sits on a Bender internal BMS bus (RS-485) and republishes the data of up to 150 BMS devices (ISOMETER, RCMS, EDS, MK800, PRC changeover modules) as Modbus/TCP input registers. Each BMS address gets its own 256-register block: device name, timestamp, alarm flags, then 4 registers per channel (float value, alarm/unit byte pair, text code). This map shows the block for BMS address 1 (channels 1-12), the test record at address 0 and the command interface.

addressing.note: Addresses are printed in hex and go on the wire as-is: the manual's example request for BMS device 1 puts 0x0100 in the start-address field. Block start = BMS address x 0x100; channel n of that device starts at block + 0x10 + 4 x (n-1). Bender notes that some clients need 1 added (process image then starts at 0x0101).

source.title: COM461MT Operating Manual - BMS Ethernet gateway for the connection of Bender devices with BMS support to Ethernet (TCP/IP) using the Modbus/TCP protocol
source.pages: pp. 25-58 (ch. 6 requests, ch. 7 process image, 7.3 reference data, 7.4 channel codes, 7.5 control commands)

notes: Only BMS device address 1 is listed. Every other device uses the same layout shifted by its address: BMS address N starts at N x 0x100 (e.g. address 3 channel 2 = 0x0314). Channel numbers in each block follow the BMS device's own channel list.
Channels 13-32 continue the 4-register pattern up to 0x008F within each block; channels 33-64 (MK800/TM800 master mode, digital only) are one byte each from 0x90 and are not listed.
Float word order: the manual states big-endian and gives the test value 12.34 at 0x0014 as words 0x4145, 0x70A4 (high word first), so ABCD is documented, not assumed.

Channel word 2 packs two bytes. High byte (AT&T): bits 0-2 alarm type (0 none, 1 prewarning, 2 device error, 4 alarm yellow LED, 5 alarm red LED), bit 6 internal test, bit 7 external test. Low byte (R&U): bits 0-4 unit (1 none, 2 ohm, 3 A, 4 V, 5 %, 6 Hz, 7 baud, 8 F, 9 H, 10 degC, 11 degF, 12 s, 13 min, 14 h, 15 day, 16 month, 30 CODE), bits 6-7 validity (0 true value, 1 true value smaller, 2 larger, 3 invalid).
When the unit is CODE the float holds an internal code, not a measurement; read the description code (word 3) and Bender's text table in ch. 7.4.
Unit ID is not specified in the manual; its example request uses unit identifier 0x01. The TCP port is not stated.
The device's own BMS address on the internal bus is 2 by factory default (range 1-99).

integration.summary: Read input registers (FC4) at BMS address x 0x100: register +0x0E tells you if the device has an alarm or has dropped off the bus, and each channel's float value sits at +0x10 + 4 x (channel-1). First read the test record at 0x0010/0x0014 (230.0 and 12.34) to prove your float word order.

minimum_registers.why: Test value 12.34 - check word order once

integration.enable: Set IP address, subnet mask, BMS address and 'Modbus control' (on/off) on the gateway's web page (factory IP 192.168.0.254, mask 255.255.0.0). Commands only work while Modbus control is enabled.
quirks: Only FC4 (read input registers) is used for data; up to 125 registers per request. FC16 is used for the command block.
Some Modbus clients need an offset of 1 (start of the process image becomes 0x0101).
Commands: always write all four words 0xFC00-0xFC03 in one FC16 request, then poll 0xFC04 until it reads 2 (ready) or 1 (error).
BMS address 0 is a simulated device holding fixed test values; no real device can use address 0.
setup: Connect a PC to the COM461MT and browse to its IP to change network settings, BMS address, time zone and NTP server.
Terminate the internal BMS bus (RS-485, 9.6 kbit/s): switch on the COM461MT's terminating switch when it sits at the end of the bus.
Run a BMS bus scan so the gateway learns the device names shown at +0x00 of each block.
gotchas: A block exists for every BMS address but only holds data for devices actually present; check the device-lost flag before trusting values.
The meaning of each channel depends on the connected Bender device type, not on the gateway.
